hints: Ask the question per column rather than per puddle: how deep is the water standing on top of column `i`?
It is the smaller of the tallest column to its left and the tallest to its right, minus its own height - and never less than zero.
Those two running maxima can each be computed in one pass, which gives an O(n) answer using O(n) space. Then ask what you would need to drop the arrays.
Walk inwards from both ends. Whichever side is currently shorter is the side whose maximum is the binding one, so that column's water is known now - and you can advance that side.
